test.name: Routes 'who is this person in the household?' to research-plan when the person's records are already extracted
test.description: Mined from issue #4670's headless replay (2026-11-26). After the first turn had extracted the household censuses, the researcher asked who Harriet Phillips is in the 1860 household and the router answered in conversation from the extracted rows, with no hand-off. Having a person's records extracted does not identify them: asking who an unidentified household member is stays a steer to research-plan on the current question, with no kinship reading and no identification in the reply.

input.user_message: /research Before we plan the searches: who would the Harriet Phillips be, in the 1860 census household?

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. The first hand-off is asserted deterministically by test_routes_to_expected_skill from the PreToolUse hook records; do not grade which callee was reached, or in what order, from the transcript.

Asking who an unidentified person in a record or household is, is a steer on the current question, not a question between steps the router answers itself and not a new question. The delegation to research-plan is plan work on the current question q_001 (a first plan here, since q_001 has none yet); a delegation that asks for a new question, or a hand-off to question-selection, is a defect.

The person's records are already extracted into the project (her census rows are in sources and assertions). That does not identify her: the router's reply that names her relationship to the household, or ranks or summarizes who she probably is from those rows, is an in-conversation identification and a defect.

Fail the router's own narration if it offers a kinship reading of the person from shared surname and age (a mother-in-law, an older sister, a cousin, a boarder), ranks such readings, or calls one the most likely. Naming what the plan will look for is fine; naming who she probably is, is not.
Fail it too if it explains away a specific detail in the record (an age or birthplace) as an enumerator or indexing error.

Every callee is stubbed and returns a denial telling the router to stop. The spawn is invisible to you, and test_routes_to_expected_skill already asserts it happened, so a reply saying the work was handed off is true even though no plan was written. Grade the router's state derivation, its honesty about what it delegated and did not do, and whether its narration stayed free of a kinship guess.
